newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil futures bolsa to launch bond, ag contracts.
newsitem.headline: Brazil futures bolsa to launch bond, ag contracts.

text.p: Brazilian futures exchange Bolsa de Mercadorias & Futuros (BM&F) will launch futures contracts this month on cotton, corn and Argentine Floating Rate Bonds, an exchange official said.
BM&F will begin trading corn contracts on November 22, while the bond and cotton contracts will be launched November 29, the bolsa's president Manoel Pires da Costa told reporters on Monday.

The Argentine bond contract will be similar to the Brazilian C-Bond contract, launched earlier this year, and will have a face value of $50,000, said Marco Aurelio Teixeira, technical superintendent at BM&F.

Teixeira said trading volume in the Argentine bond contracts is not expected to match that of Brazilian C-Bonds, which currently trade between 2,500 and 4,500 contracts daily, worth $250 million and $450 million.
Trade in the Argentine contract would be more active if the Central Bank allowed Argentine investors to trade it without paying a financial operations tax (IOF), he said.
Teixeira noted Argentine investors are only allowed to trade derivatives through special accounts for non-residents, paying a seven percent IOF.
The launch of the Argentine bond contracts is part of the bolsa's strategy to move internationally and consolidate its position in the Mercosur region, the BM&F president said.
BM&F is the world's fourth largest futures exchange. Total turnover in October was $552 billion, against $242.6 billion the same month last year.
